idiom_name: Playwright .NET POM: class with readonly ILocator fields over IPage (xUnit/NUnit)
implementation_notes: Playwright .NET documents the page object as a class that wraps an IPage and exposes its own API over ILocator fields created once in the constructor: locators are lazy and re-resolved on every action, so the class never caches DOM state, and the test constructs the page from the fixture's IPage. What replaces the classic reflective PageFactory - absent from Selenium .NET's current support project, which carries the LoadableComponent<T> family instead - is ordinary readonly fields plus the driver's own auto-waiting; xUnit or NUnit owns the browser fixture lifetime. Add navigation methods returning the next page class so the flow stays typed.
pitfalls: Do not revive the PageFactory idiom by caching IWebElement values in fields: element references captured once go stale after a re-render - keep ILocator (lazy) or re-query per action.

xUnit constructs the test class per test while NUnit reuses fixtures: sharing one page object or one IPage across parallel tests makes results order-dependent, so scope the browser context to the test.
An async page method that is not awaited (or that returns void) makes the test race the UI; every action and navigation method is Task-returning and awaited.

variants.name: Selenium .NET: hand-written page classes with LoadableComponent<T>
variants.implementation_notes: Without PageFactory, a Selenium .NET page is a plain class holding IWebDriver plus By locators and service methods; Selenium.Support's LoadableComponent<T> is available when a page or component must verify that it loaded (Load() calls the overridden ExecuteLoad and EvaluateLoadedStatus, and throws LoadableComponentException otherwise). The cost is that element lookup, waits and staleness handling are yours: every method re-queries through the driver or WebDriverWait instead of keeping WebElement references, and the fixture disposes the driver.
pitfalls: LoadableComponent<T>.Load() throws LoadableComponentException when IsLoaded stays false: an always-false EvaluateLoadedStatus (or a slow page without a wait) turns every test into a load failure.
WebElement values are not re-resolved: caching them in fields reintroduces staleness, so every method re-queries through the driver (or wraps the lookup in a wait).
The driver is not thread-safe; parallel NUnit/xUnit tests need a driver per test, disposed in the fixture, not a static page object holding one session.
